films.title: Boatbuilders
films.synopsis: Premiering at the Venice Film Festival, Sundance Award-winning director Luke Lorentzen’s beautifully observed documentary follows craftspeople of Brooklin Boat Yard across four seasons as they transform raw timber into a magnificent 56-foot sailboat—a celebration of craftsmanship, community, and purpose.
films.fullDescription:
On the rugged coast of Maine, the craftspeople of the Brooklin Boat Yard practice an increasingly rare art: building extraordinary wooden boats by hand. Over four changing seasons, Sundance Award-winning director Luke Lorentzen follows more than 60 skilled workers as they transform Douglas fir, mahogany, and cedar into a breathtaking 56-foot sailboat.
From the first precise cuts and carefully fitted joints to the vessel’s exhilarating maiden voyage, Boatbuilders finds beauty, humor, and quiet drama in the painstaking process of creating something built to last. Along the way, Lorentzen captures the close-knit community surrounding the yard and the generations of knowledge embedded in this time-honored craft.
Premiering at the Venice Film Festival, Boatbuilders is a warm, visually stunning meditation on craftsmanship, community, and the profound satisfaction that comes from slowing down, paying attention, and taking pride in a job well done.

films.fullDescription: Oscar-winning filmmaker Peter Farrelly (Green Book) returns with this stirring true story of ambition, perseverance, and one of Hollywood’s most improbable breakthroughs. In a star-making performance, Anthony Ippolito disappears into the role of a young Sylvester Stallone, then an unknown and struggling actor who writes Rocky and refuses lucrative offers unless he is allowed to play the lead himself. What follows is an extraordinary battle against the Hollywood establishment that ultimately produces the 1976 Best Picture winner and transforms Stallone into an international star. Featuring Matt Dillon, Stephan James, and Tracy Letts, I Play Rocky combines prestige filmmaking with irresistible crowd appeal, celebrating artistic conviction, risk, and the creation of an American screen icon. As children, Fujino and the reclusive Kyomoto are brought together by a shared passion for drawing, their early competition gradually deepening into a powerful artistic bond. As they grow into aspiring manga artists, the joy of creating together is tested by the unpredictability of life. Shot on 35mm and unfolding across the seasons, LOOK BACK is infused with the warmth and emotional precision that define Kore-eda’s work. films.fullDescription: Manuela Martelli follows Chile ’76 with a slow-burn mystery set in the Andes. Featuring Saskia Rosendahl, Maia Rae Domagala, and Jakub Gierszał, the film uses a child’s perspective to uncover adult secrets and the lingering unease of post-Pinochet Chile. A Cannes Un Certain Regard selection. Chile´s Official Submission to the Academy Awards for Best International Feature. A Kino Lorber Release.

films.title: Minotaur
films.synopsis: Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev’s riveting, razor-sharp tale of personal, patriarchal, and governmental corruption follows a wealthy CEO who begins to suspect his wife is having an extramarital affair.
films.fullDescription: Winner of the Cannes Grand Prix, Andrey Zvyagintsev’s gripping return to filmmaking is a razor-sharp drama of jealousy, power, and corruption. A wealthy executive’s suspicion that his wife is having an affair opens onto a broader portrait of patriarchal entitlement and political rot. Made by one of contemporary cinema’s great moral anatomists, Minotaur is tense, elegant, and devastatingly relevant. A MUBI release.

films.title: Mouse
films.synopsis: Mouse stars Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Chloe Coleman, Sophie Okonedo, David Hyde Pierce, and Iman Vellani in a tender, funny 2002-set story of friendship, family, and growing apart.
films.fullDescription: Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, the team behind Saint Frances and Ghostlight, return with a tender 2002-set coming-of-age drama. Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Chloe Coleman play longtime friends whose relationship fractures as adulthood approaches, while Sophie Okonedo gives a key performance as the mother who becomes an unexpected emotional refuge. David Hyde Pierce and Iman Vellani round out the ensemble. Warm, perceptive, and quietly funny. An IFC Films Release.

films.title: Nuisance Bear
films.synopsis: Sundance U.S. Grand Jury Prize winner Nuisance Bear transforms a familiar polar-bear story into a visually daring documentary about survival, spectacle, tourism, Indigenous perspective, and human coexistence in a rapidly changing Arctic.
films.fullDescription: Winner of Sundance’s U.S. Grand Jury Prize for Documentary, Nuisance Bear expands the filmmakers’ acclaimed short into a formally daring feature about polar bears and the humans who profit from, monitor, photograph, and redirect them. Guided in part by an Inuit narrator, the film turns a familiar nature subject into a provocative study of spectacle, survival, and coexistence in a rapidly changing Arctic. A MUBI release.

films.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
films.synopsis: In 1972, filmmaker William Greaves gathered legendary Harlem Renaissance figures for an extraordinary conversation; more than fifty years later, his son completes the cinematic time capsule. Official Selection Sundance, Cannes and New York Film Festival.
films.fullDescription: Legendary filmmaker William Greaves assembled artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers connected to the Harlem Renaissance for a remarkable 1972 gathering. Decades later, his son David Greaves has completed the project, creating an intimate living history of Black artistic and intellectual life. An NYFF selection and a rare archival treasure, the film is both a cultural document and a moving act of preservation across generations. A NEON release.

films.title: Paper Tiger
films.synopsis: Cannes and New York Film Festival opening night selection PAPER TIGER stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson in James Gray’s gripping 1980s New York drama, an ambitious story of brotherhood, crime, family, and the devastating cost of chasing the American dream.
films.fullDescription: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson headline James Gray’s gripping 1980s New York thriller, the Opening Night selection of NYFF. Teller plays a Queens family man drawn into a shady scheme by his former-cop brother, played by Driver, with devastating consequences at home. Rich in period detail and escalating tension, this masterwork turns crime, pollution, brotherhood, and the American dream into emotionally charged drama. A NEON release.

films.title: Possible Love
films.synopsis: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding drama of class, marriage, labor conflict, ethics, and emotional betrayal. South Korea´s Academy Award Entry, Best International Feature.
films.fullDescription: Lee Chang-dong returns with a major ensemble drama starring Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Zo In-sung. A wealthy documentary filmmaker begins filming a working-class couple still reeling from a violently suppressed labor dispute, creating shifting alliances, resentments, and ethical dilemmas. South Korea’s 2027 Oscar submission is a richly layered study of class, marriage, and the morality of looking at other people’s lives. A Netflix release.

films.title: RADIOHEART: The Drive and Times of DJ Kevin Cole
films.synopsis: From Minneapolis dance floors to Seattle’s KEXP, legendary DJ Kevin Cole looks back on fifty years of music, community, addiction, recovery, and the transformative power of radio.
films.fullDescription: Music lovers will feel this one. RADIOHEART traces music impresario Kevin Cole’s extraordinary path from Minneapolis’ First Avenue to 25 influential years at KEXP, blending archival footage, animation, and a killer soundtrack with interviews featuring Bob Mould, Jimmy Jam, Jessica Dobson, and more. Winner of Best of Fest at Minneapolis St. Paul and a standout at the Seattle International Film Festival, it is an uplifting portrait of music as connection, healing, and community.

films.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
films.synopsis: Winner of the Best Documentary prize at Cannes, filmmaker and actress Pegah Ahangarani turns her own family archive into a deeply personal chronicle of Iran’s long struggle for freedom. Drawing on home movies, street-protest footage, newspapers, sketches, photographs, and recorded voices, Ahangarani intertwines her life story with more than four decades of political upheaval.
films.fullDescription: Pegah Ahangarani’s powerful first feature uses home movies, street footage, newspapers, animation, and recorded voices to connect one family’s history to more than four decades of Iranian political struggle. Structured around five people who embody different forms of resistance, the film moves from 1979 to the present. A Cannes Special Screening and Golden Eye–recognized documentary, Rehearsals for a Revolution is personal history transformed into urgent political cinema. A Sony Pictures Classics release.

films.title: Rose
films.synopsis: Berlin’s Silver Bear winner Sandra Hüller fully inhabits the daunting role of a 17th-century woman who disguises herself as a male soldier, only to continue the ruse after battle, in this enthralling fable of faith and social intolerance. Austria’s Academy Award Entry, Best International Feature.
films.fullDescription: Sandra Hüller won the Berlin Silver Bear for Best Leading Performance for her extraordinary turn as a woman who lives as a man after the Thirty Years’ War. Markus Schleinzer’s austere black-and-white drama follows Rose into a Protestant community where a male identity allows property, marriage, and freedom—until rumors begin to close in. Austria’s 2027 Oscar submission, this MUBI release is a gripping fable of gender, faith, and intolerance. A MUBI release.

films.title: Union Town
films.synopsis: Two-time Oscar winner Barbara Kopple returns to labor documentary with Venice Film Festival documentary following UPS, Amazon, and app-based delivery workers organizing across New York in a timely fight for solidarity and power.
films.fullDescription: Two-time Oscar winner Barbara Kopple completes a labor trilogy begun with Harlan County U.S.A. and American Dream. Filmed over three years, Union Town follows essential delivery workers across UPS, Amazon, and app-based bike services as they organize in New York City. Premiering at Venice, the documentary captures a new generation of labor activism while asking what solidarity means in an economy increasingly divided between those with power and those fighting for it.

films.title: We Are The Shaggs
films.synopsis: Orcas Island's own Ken Kwapis dramatizes the stranger-than-fiction story of The Shaggs, three sisters pushed into a band by their father whose failed musical dream later became outsider-art legend—funny, odd, and unexpectedly moving.
films.fullDescription: Ken Kwapis brings the improbable story of The Shaggs to the screen: three sisters pushed into a band by their determined father, only to record music later embraced as outsider-art legend. Strange, funny, and ultimately touching, the film celebrates creative innocence, family dynamics, and the unpredictable ways failed dreams can become cultural mythology. A natural fit for music lovers and audiences who adore true stories stranger than fiction.

films.title: You Found Me
films.synopsis: A woman’s carefully ordered life is upended by an unexpected romantic encounter in Alice Vial’s warm French comedy about timing, vulnerability, and the surprises love still has in store.
films.fullDescription: Alice Vial’s polished French romantic comedy brings wit and emotional intelligence to the familiar question of what happens when love arrives at the wrong—or perhaps exactly the right—moment. With a brisk 98-minute runtime and an accessible mix of humor, romance, and character, You Found Me offers an easy audience entry point into contemporary French cinema.
